title.narrative: Provide integrated life-saving WASH services to the deserving hard to hard- and rural areas in Jamame district (flagship pilot to mitigate drought)

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThe proposed SRDI flagship WASH project will directly be implemented in Jamame district, the project aims to provide integrated WASH, nutrition, Health life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable communities in Jamame district hard to reach rural areas, this is intended to address the impacts of worsening drought conditions and help mitigate displacement in Jamame district. According to the 2025 PiN, Jamame district hosts approximately 49,690 people in IPC Phase 3+, including 1,110 rural residents, 33,300 IDPs, and 28,280 urban populations, the district reports critical nutritional indicators with GAM at 13%, MAM at 11.4%, and SAM at 1.8%, this coupled with poor health and WASH infrastructure as well as poor livelihood in the district.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtSRDI aims to implement key community-priority initiative through an integrated approach across sector. However, the project activities prioritization are based on the results of the community engagement process and its outcomes, this is according to the resultant outcome from the community engagement and problem basket ranking at the end of the engagement process. Throughout the project design, implementation and monitoring phase SRDI will ensure thorough community decision making and participation through inclusive community engagement mechanisms that will ensure representation of women, men, boys, girls as well as persons with disabilities. Community consultations will be conducted in safe and accessible spaces, using culturally appropriate communication methods. The project will integrate clear safeguarding measures to mitigate risks of abuse, exploitation (including SEA) and violence (including GBV), This will include training staff on protection principles, establishing confidential and accessible reporting channels, and enforcing a strict code of conduct. Continuous monitoring will be carried out using protection-focused indicators, in alignment with the Somalia Protection Mainstreaming in the SHF Programme Manual. The project will coordinate closely with protection actors to ensure that all interventions are safe, inclusive and responsive to emerging protection risks. SRDI project will be guided by the flagship initiative strategy, which places crisis-affected communities at the center of the response, ensuring that their priorities drive humanitarian action through decentralized coordination structures this approach guarantees that all activities reflect community-led priorities.ltbrgt ltbrgtSRDI will collaborate with the community -based structure and representative by initially mapping the community existing leadership structure as well as informal networks within Jamame district, this includes minorities and disabilities association for inclusive decision. Through ongoing dialogue and participatory planning, SRDI will engage these structures to identify barriers to inclusion and jointly design strategies to overcome them. Capacity-building initiatives covering protection principles, inclusive practices, conflict resolution and accountability will be delivered in local languages and through accessible formats to ensure meaningful participation of all community membersltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtSRDI is a key humanitarian actor in Lower Juba with ongoing SHF La Niña interventions, including a recently concluded WASH program in Afmadow district, as well as currently SHF standard allocation 1-2025 in Buale middle Juba and is strategically positioned within the region. SRDI concluded nutrition activities in Kismayo border locations of Jamame. However its established presence and community trust will facilitate the timely and effective implementation of interventions to meet the district’s pressing needs.lt/spangtlt/pgt
